questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between CASE and IF/ELSE?
options: IF/ELSE can be used inside a SELECT list; CASE cannot
CASE can only be used in stored procedures; IF/ELSE cannot
CASE is an expression that evaluates to a value; IF/ELSE is a statement that controls which block of code runs
They are functionally identical, just different syntax
questions.explain: This distinction was first introduced in Lesson 7 and is central to understanding control flow vs. expressions.

questions.q: Can IF be used inside a SELECT list the way CASE can?
options: Only when combined with a subquery
Yes, IF works identically to CASE inside SELECT
No — IF decides between running one chunk of T-SQL or another, it doesn't produce a value inline
Only in SQL Server 2019 and later
questions.explain: This is exactly why CASE and IF/ELSE serve different purposes despite superficial similarity.

Creates a new variable

questions.explain: PRINT is useful for demonstration and debugging, distinct from returning query results.

questions.q: In a chain of ELSE IF conditions, when is each one evaluated?
options: Only if every condition above it was false, evaluated top to bottom
In random order
All conditions are evaluated simultaneously
Only the last ELSE IF is ever checked
questions.explain: This mirrors the top-to-bottom evaluation order from searched CASE (Lesson 8), just applied to control flow.

questions.q: What kind of expression does an IF condition evaluate?
options: Only a column name, with no comparison allowed
IF cannot evaluate expressions, only literal TRUE/FALSE values
A predicate, exactly like a WHERE condition
A CASE expression specifically
questions.explain: IF's condition is evaluated the same way a WHERE clause's predicate is (Lesson 20's concept), just used for branching instead of filtering.
